parsed.why: Strong state-level nondiscrimination, facility, and healthcare protections improve on the national baseline, but national document and entry screening remain serious exposures; youth-care coverage is also being suspended, and custody protections have a history of litigation.

Broad public-accommodation protections with an enforcement route, accessible state IDs, and protections for travelling families materially mitigate the national regime. No local universal hostile exposure is documented; violence evidence is comparatively reassuring but not proof of safety.

State protections include a shield against out-of-state care enforcement and broad nondiscrimination rules. These improve on the national baseline, though documented birth-sex custody placement and harm, even if dated, temper the rating.

A sanctuary law, protective facility rulings, and state protections mitigate national restrictions, though visitor coverage of the sanctuary law is unclear. Two recent killings are concerning but lack denominator or background-rate evidence of a targeted pattern.

The national regime is compounded by state birth-sex facility restrictions, marker limits, and explicit judicial hostility, with little recourse outside some municipalities. These add substantial exposure beyond the national baseline; the dated prosecuted killing does not establish a current pattern.
